items.title: महिला पत्रकारों ने लगाए दिल्ली पुलिस पर हिरासत में मारपीट के गंभीर आरोप

items.title: ‘Saffron hooliganism’ coverage FIRs: HC asks for no coercive action against Anandabazar Patrika journalists
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court has asked the West Bengal government to assure that no coercive steps would be taken against Anandabazar Patrika journalists facing FIRs over the newspaper’s use of the phrase “saffron hooliganism”, as long as they cooperate with the notices issued to them, LiveLaw reported . The first case was filed on August 28 at the Bowbazar police station in Kolkata over a complaint by Shastri Maharaj, described as a Hindu monk. It objected to the term, ‘gerua gundami’ that translates into ‘saffron hooliganism’ that featured in reports by the publication on violent clashes that erupted at Jadavpur University earlier last month. Several press associations have demanded the immediate withdrawal of the FIRs. On Thursday, the state, represented by the Additional Advocate General Rajdeep Mazumdar, gave the assurance the court asked for after Senior Advocate S N Mookherjee, assisted by Advocates Arunabha Deb and Ashika Daga, flagged the FIRs. Mookherjee reportedly said the cases had been initiated on the allegation of incitement as if journalists had demeaned sanyasis across the country. He also told the court that the outlet’s office had been painted saffron by protestors. Reports had earlier mentioned videos showing two men painting two pillars at the main entrance of the office while several police personnel stand by. Several other saffron-clad men had gathered at the spot, raising slogans including “Bhagwa ka apmaan nahi sahega” (“We will not tolerate the insult of Bhagwa”) and “Anandabazar Patrika haye haye”. The court asked Mookherjee whether he was familiar with the expression “saffron vandalism”. It also referred to the newspaper’s front page. Mookherjee submitted that the matter was not political but concerned the journalists. The Additional Advocate General asked whether the journalists could claim any special protection. Mookherjee clarified that he was not claiming any special privilege. The court then sought an assurance that no steps would be taken until the matter came up for consideration. “Comply with the notice, no steps will be taken. If anything happens, bring it to my notice,” the court said, according to LiveLaw . items.title: Migration is not a crisis or a cure-all. It just needs to be managed
items.summary: Migration is one of the defining forces of the 21st century. It changes economies, societies, families and individual lives. Yet public debate often reduces it to a deceptively simple question, one which drives division and anger: are you for migration or against it? That is the wrong question. Human beings have always moved. They move for work, family, education, safety, adventure and a better life. Sometimes they move once and settle permanently. Often they move several times, maintain connections across borders, or eventually return home. Migration is rarely just an individual calculation about wages. Families and communities shape decisions. Social networks make some destinations easier to reach than others. Recruiters, universities and employers actively encourage mobility. Historical ties, languages, trade relationships and colonial legacies create migration pathways that can persist for generations. And beneath all these explanations lies something more basic: human beings have always sought movement, opportunity and change. Migration transforms lives For many migrants, moving dramatically improves living standards. Crossing from a poor country to a wealthy one can multiply earnings several times over. Migration can also provide access to safer communities, better education, healthcare and political freedoms. But migration can create serious vulnerabilities too. Once people cross borders, responsibility for protecting them becomes blurred. Migrants can become vulnerable to exploitative employers, dishonest recruitment agents, smugglers and traffickers. Temporary workers are especially exposed when their visa status depends heavily on a particular employer. Migration also affects the places people leave behind. Emigration can deprive poorer countries of skilled doctors, nurses, engineers and other professionals. Rural areas may lose population. Families can spend years separated. But migrants also send money, knowledge and investment home. Remittances have become one of the largest financial flows into many developing countries, often exceeding both foreign aid and foreign investment. Diasporas can create trade links, businesses, professional networks and opportunities that span borders. Migration therefore creates risks and rewards on both sides of the journey. items.title: Sylvia Karpagam’s ‘The Meat of the Matter’ calls for freeing India’s plate from prejudice
items.summary: In modern India, the kitchen has become a battlefield for state-sanctioned majoritarianism. While the right to safe, nutritious food is a fundamental prerequisite for human survival, public policy under the current dispensation has weaponised dietary habits to enforce social hierarchies. From the institutional exclusion of eggs in school midday meals to targeted communal bans on meat vendors, what ends up on an Indian's plate is increasingly engineered by prejudice rather than public health science. This toxic overlap of nutrition science, state overreach, and caste bias forms the volatile core of Dr Sylvia Karpagam’s The Meat of the Matter: How the Politics of Food Shapes Our Health . In this extensively researched and cogently argued book, Dr Karpagam makes a compelling case that the health of Indians would be best served by ditching superstition and prejudice in favour of a science-driven, evidence-based approach. Essential to this enterprise is the political will to acknowledge a fact contrary to popular misconception: the vast majority of Indians are meat-eaters. Vegetarianism – which in India typically includes the consumption of milk and dairy products – is a niche dietary practice of a minority. Yet, as the book makes plain, this minority sits at the apex of social and political power structures, using its privileged position to allow personal prejudices to dictate bad public policy. The Meat of the Matter is a slim, 213-page, eminently readable volume. The author and publishers manage to pack a vast amount of information into a compact format through two deliberate choices. First, they omit a traditional index. Second, they host the extensive annotations and over 600 references on the publisher's website, accessible via a QR code printed in the book. While keen researchers might initially miss a physical index and student readers must take an extra step to access the source citations, the volume stands perfectly for the general reader as a self-contained powerhouse of facts, logic, and sound argument. Dr Karpagam systematically takes the reader through the foundational science of human nutrition. She addresses what infants and growing children require for optimal cognitive and physical development and what adults need to consume to remain resilient against infections, sustain energy, and lead productive lives. items.summary: केंद्र सरकार में पूर्व अतिरिक्त सचिव आशीष जोशी को बुधवार सुबह नेहरू पार्क में टहलते समय सादे कपड़ों में आए दो लोग जोशी की कार में बैठाकर अपने साथ ले गए. देर शाम तक उनके बारे में कोई जानकारी नहीं थी कि उन्हें कौन, कहां और क्यों ले गया. जोशी के साथ सुबह की सैर पर मौजूद दो लोगों ने बताया कि दोनों आदमी खुद को दिल्ली पुलिस से बता रहे थे. लेकिन परिवार को भी इस संबंध में कोई सूचना नहीं दी गई. बाद में यह जानकारी सामने आई कि उन्हें न्यू फ्रेंड्स कॉलोनी (एनएफसी) स्थित स्पेशल सेल के कार्यालय ले जाया गया. दिल्ली पुलिस के एक अधिकारी ने न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री को बताया कि आशीष जोशी के खिलाफ स्पेशल सेल में पहले से एक मामला दर्ज है, उसी के सिलसिले में उन्हें पूछताछ के लिए लाया गया था. अधिकारी ने साथ ही यह भी स्पष्ट किया, “उन्हें गिरफ्तार नहीं किया गया था. पूछताछ के बाद उन्हें छोड़ दिया गया है.” एनएफसी थाने पहुंचे आशीष जोशी के एक सहयोगी ने न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री से उनके रिहा होने की पुष्टि की. उन्होंने बताया, “जोशी को दूसरे गेट से बाहर निकाला गया. हम दूसरे गेट पर लगातार उनका इंतजार कर रहे थे.” इस दौरान शाम को जोशी की पत्नी, बेटी और कुछ सहयोगी स्पेशल सेल के दफ्तर के बाहर मौजूद थे. हमने उनकी पत्नी से बात करने की कोशिश की तो बताया गया कि वह काफी परेशान हैं और बात करने की स्थिति में नहीं हैं. जोशी के सहयोगी के मुताबिक, वो अपनी गाड़ी से स्पेशल सेल के कार्यालय से निकले. निकलने के कुछ देर बाद उन्होंने अपनी पत्नी को वीडियो कॉल किया और कहा, “मैं निकल गया हूं और घर पहुंच रहा हूं. आप लोग भी घर आ जाइए.” इसके बाद परिवार के सभी सदस्य घर लौट गए. घर पहुंचने के बाद आशीष जोशी ने एक्स पर पोस्ट कर बताया, “अभी घर पहुंचा हूं. दिल्ली स्पेशल सेल ने मुझे घर छोड़ दिया है. बाकी जानकारी बाद में साझा करूंगा.” आशीष जोशी मोती बाग में रहते हैं और रोजाना सैर के लिए नेहरू पार्क जाते हैं. बुधवार को भी वह अपनी गाड़ी से पार्क पहुंचे थे. इसी दौरान जब वह दोस्तों के साथ टहल रहे थे, तभी सादे कपड़ों में दो लोग आए और उन्हें अपने साथ ले गए. उनके सहयोगी ने हमें बताया कि इस मामले में परिवार को कोई पूर्व नोटिस नहीं दिया गया. आशीष जोशी के खिलाफ कोई एफआईआर दर्ज हुई है तो उसकी जानकारी भी परिवार को नहीं दी गई है. दूसरी ओर जैसे ही आशीष जोशी के साथ हुई घटना की ख़बर फैला, सोशल मीडिया पर सवाल उठने लगे. कांग्रेस नेता संदीप दीक्षित ने एक्स पर लिखा , “मुझे इस बारे में तब पता चला, जब सुबह उनकी पत्नी ने मुझसे बात की. हम सुबह 10 बजे से ही उनका पता लगाने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं, लेकिन कोई सुराग नहीं मिला है. हम बहुत परेशान हैं और दिल्ली पुलिस को जल्द से जल्द हमें बताना चाहिए कि उन्हें कहां ले जाया गया है.” इस बीच, आशीष जोशी का एक्स पर किया गया एक पुराना पोस्ट भी चर्चा में है. हालांकि, वह पोस्ट अब एक्स से हटा दिया गया है. हमने आशीष जोशी से भी संपर्क किया.

items.title: The enigma of BlueKraft: The narrative factory behind Brand Modi
items.summary: Read the previous instalments of this series here and here . On September 24, 2025, thousands of people were on the streets of Leh demanding statehood for Ladakh, jobs and constitutional protection for a fragile high-altitude ecology. Within 72 hours, that was no longer the conversation. A commentator named Richa Dwivedi had appeared on a platform called New India Junction to argue that the activist Sonam Wangchuk had inflamed the crowd by invoking the Arab Spring and Nepal’s Gen Z protests, after which the mob turned violent – and that Congress councillors had been “caught on camera” egging protesters toward stone-pelting and bandh calls. Around the same time another commentator, Ojas Bhandari, was posting videos calling Wangchuk “anti-national” and noting that he had reportedly been in Islamabad shortly before the Pahalgam attack. The trending question soon was whether Sonam Wangchuk was a foreign asset. Then on July 20 this year, on the day of the ‘Chalo Sansad’ march, another content creator Garima Upreti questioned the violence at the Cockroach Janta Party protest and tagged Wangchuk to say “Look at your goons. Is this a national capital or Kashmir?” Trace the accounts that drove the pivot, and the trail runs, again and again, to a single organisation – one registered, improbably, under “human health and social care services,” half-owned by a tech millionaire who says he wants nothing more to do with it, and followed, personally, on X, by the Prime Minister of India. Its name is BlueKraft. And the question it has never answered is the simplest one of all: who pays for it all? One address, many masks BlueKraft does not look like much from the outside, which is the point. Its work surfaces under names that suggest grassroots energy or neutral journalism – New India Junction , The True Picture, Know The Nation, Modi Story – and almost never under its own. National Investigation Agency] . A Division Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Ravinder Dudeja held that both the accused had already suffered a custody of almost 5 years pending trial and there is no chance of the trial ending soon. “We have also minutely perused the allegations against the appellant Kamran Ashraf Reshi, as also the material relied upon by the NIA against him. While we refrain from giving a detailed account of the same, as we fear that it may prejudice the trial, we are of the opinion that given the long period of incarceration of the appellant juxtaposed against the material alleged against him by the NIA, the appellant has been able to make out a case for being released on bail,” the Court said in Reshi’s case. In Aziz’s case, the Bench observed that while the National Investigation Agency (NIA) said there is some prima facie material, she still has an arguable case for grant of bail. items.summary: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has held that the Trustees’ Association of India (TAI) and three debenture trustee companies indulged in cartelisation by collectively fixing the minimum fees to be charged for debenture trusteeship services. The trustee companies found guilty were IDBI Trusteeship Services Limited, Axis Trustee Services Limited and SBI CAP Trustee Company Limited. The CCI found that the entities had violated Sections 3(3)(a) and 3(3)(b) of the Competition Act by fixing benchmark prices and limiting the supply of debenture trusteeship services during financial years 2020-21 and 2021-22. “ Such collective fixing of minimum price/fee by OP-1, for the provision of debenture trusteeship services, and other follow-on actions prevented independent commercial decision making by the DTs and amounted to cartelisation .” However, the Commission did not impose any monetary penalty. It took into account that the Association had no income during the period of contravention and that the three trustee companies had charged fees below the benchmark price in several cases. items.title: Delhi HC appoints advocate Gautam Bhatia as amicus curiae in Janhvi Kapoor personality rights suit
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday appointed advocate Gautam Bhatia as amicus curiae in a personality rights suit filed by Bollywood actor Janhvi Kapoor. The Court's appointment of Bhatia as amicus comes against the backdrop of its earlier concerns over the scope of personality rights claims. The matter was listed before Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani . During the hearing, counsel appearing for Kapoor submitted that the URLs identified as infringing had been segregated and categorised in accordance with the directions issued by the Court during an earlier hearing . The counsel also sought early consideration of the categories for the purpose of passing an interim order. Taking note of the submissions, the Court ordered, "Considering the issues involved, this court considers it appropriate to appoint advocate Gautam Bhatia as amicus to assist the court." Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani On August 11, the Court had directed the takedown of online content concerning Kapoor that was ex facie pornographic, obscene, prurient or lascivious and appeared to directly monetise her personality rights. However, the Court had declined to order a blanket takedown of fan pages. It had observed that such a direction could have implications for free speech. It had also questioned the contours of personality rights in the digital age and had asked lawyers to assist it in bringing “some sanity” to the concept. Advocate Gautam Bhatia Kapoor's suit seeks removal of more than 5,000 webpages and social media posts allegedly involving pornographic AI-generated content, impersonation, fake booking agencies and chatbots that commercially exploited her personality traits without consent. The matter will be heard next on September 22 for considering Kapoor's plea for interim relief.

items.title: Bombay High Court grants actress Shruti Haasan interim relief on plea against AI deepfakes
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has passed an interim order in favor of actress Shruti Haasan on her plea seeking directions to restrain the publication of artificial intelligence (AI) generated and other content that violate her personality rights by misusing her image or likeness. Haasan had approached the Court seeking the protection of her personality and publicity rights, which she contended were being violated through AI-generated deepfakes that use her image without permission, manipulated videos, unauthorised commercial endorsements, and unlicensed merchandise. Justice Madhav Jamdar , in an interim order, recognised the severe harm caused by such digital manipulation of one's image and the rapid spread of deepfakes online. "There is substance in the contention raised by the plaintiff (Haasan) that the continuing dissemination of AI-generated deepfakes, manipulated images, chatbots, and other infringing content has caused and continues to cause irreparable injury to the plaintiff's goodwill, reputation, and commercial interests. Such injury cannot be adequately compensated by monetary damages alone, as once deepfake content is disseminated across the internet, it is capable of unlimited replication and circulation, resulting in permanent dilution of the plaintiff's personality rights and public image," the Court observed. Justice Madhav Jamdar Justice Jamdar highlighted the constitutional backing of personality and privacy rights, emphasising that unauthorised digital manipulations encroach upon fundamental freedoms guaranteed under the Constitution of India. "The material on record clearly shows that (Haasan's) personality rights, publicity rights, and moral rights are violated by creation of said morphed, deepfake, and/or superimposed contents comprising the morphed plaintiff's images, photographs, and videos. (Haasan's) personality rights and publicity rights are protected by Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution of India, that is, the right of freedom of speech and expression. The right to life and personal liberty, including the right to privacy, are protected by Article 21 of the Constitution of India. The right to life as contemplated under Article 21 of the Constitution of India includes the right to live with dignity. Thus, a very strong prima facie case is made out," the Bench held. items.title: Change the date of anti-reservation protest: Delhi High Court to Kshatriya Karni Sena
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to pass any immediate direction on a plea by Kshatriya Karni Sena seeking permission to hold a demonstration against reservation and the University Grants Commission (UGC) regulations at Jantar Mantar on September 6. Justice Amit Mahajan remarked that such a permission could not be granted by the Court without hearing the Delhi Police, which had rejected Karni Sena's request. The Court also remarked that the organisation may consider changing the date of the protest from September 6 to some other date. "Change the date of the protest. What is so sacrosanct about the date? If the police is not agreeing on a particular date. You do it on another day. I can’t permit you without hearing them (police)," the Court remarked. The petitioner told the Court that they have already changed the date of the demonstration once and that it was the second time this was being done. It was stated that this was a padyatra (walk) which would culminate at Jantar Mantar. However, the Court said that it will hear the matter after considering the response of the Delhi Police. Therefore, the Court listed the case for further consideration on September 9. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court The plea was filed by Dr Raj Shekhawat, head of the Kshatriya Karni Sena, challenging the Delhi Police decision to deny permission to the group to hold a peaceful demonstration at Jantar Mantar on September 6. It was stated that the organisation was planning to protest against reservation policies and the University Grants Commission regulations. In his plea, Shekhawat stated that he had sought permission through a written application dated August 27, undertaking to comply with all lawful directions and reasonable conditions. However, police authorities rejected the request on August 28, citing ongoing preparations for the BRICS Summit. Shekhawat argued that the rejection was legally unsustainable, pointing out that the BRICS Summit is scheduled for September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, six days after the proposed demonstration, and that Jantar Mantar and Bharat Mandapam are geographically distinct locations. The petitioner also offered an express undertaking that no procession would be taken out from Jantar Mantar or moved towards Bharat Mandapam or any BRICS-related security route. items.title: Supreme Court scraps ₹425 crore penalty over fake citations, AI hallucinations in customs order
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside a ₹425.28 crore customs penalty imposed on a diamond trader after finding that the adjudicating officer had relied on non-existent cases, fake citations and legal propositions hallucinated by artificial intelligence (AI). items.title: More renewable energy disputes will fall outside regulators, go to arbitration: Gourab Banerji
items.summary: India’s rapid expansion of renewable energy will lead to a larger number of disputes falling outside electricity regulators and being resolved through arbitration, Senior Advocate Gourab Banerji has said. Banerji, President of the Arbitration Bar of India (ABI), said that while tariff disputes would necessarily remain within the regulatory framework, renewable-energy projects were generating several other categories of disputes capable of arbitration. “Because of renewable energy being such a big player, I think a large number of the disputes will now fall outside the regulator .” He cited EPC contractor disputes, supply disputes, operation and maintenance disputes, storage and performance disputes as well as shareholder disputes. Banerji said he preferred arbitration or mediation backed by technical experts rather than requiring parties to approach regulators for every dispute. “ I am actually more comfortable with arbitration plus experts or mediation plus experts as opposed to going to the regulator for each and everything .” The discussion was part of “Investing in India’s Future: Powering Growth Through Energy, Infrastructure & Legal Certainty” , held during Singapore Convention Week 2026 at Maxwell Chambers. Vinita Negi & Ors.] The suit also names tech companies like Meta and Reddit, alongside Deccan Chronicle Holdings Limited, as defendants . items.title: 'Hing' is a spice: Bombay High Court allows Nashik APMC to levy market fee
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has held that the 'Hing' (asafoetida) falls within the statutory entry of मसाल्याचे पदार्थ (spices) under a notification issued by the State government in 2005 [The Nashik Agricultural Produce Market Committee v. NG Thakkar & Sons & Ors.] Justice Amit Borkar thus set aside a September 2014 order of the Maharashtra government and an October 2011 order of the Director of Marketing, which had restrained the Nashik Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) from collecting market fees on Hing on the ground that it was not explicitly named in the statutory list. The Court held that the APMC was entitled to levy market fees on Hing under the Maharashtra Agricultural Produce Marketing (Development & Regulation) Act. “It is held that 'Hing' or 'Asafoetida' is covered by the expression 'मसाल्याचे पदार्थ' in the Notification dated 8 December 2005. The Petitioner is consequently entitled to levy and recover market fee in accordance with Section 31 of the Said Act,” the Court said on September 1. Justice Amit Borkar The Court examined statutory frameworks, including the Spices Board Act, the Customs Tariff Act and food safety standards to hold that Indian law consistently treats Hing as a spice. "Once it is accepted that 'Asafoetida' is a spice, there is no sufficient reason in the material before the Court to exclude Hing from the general expression 'मसाल्याचे पदार्थ' merely because its individual name is not separately repeated in the Schedule," the Bench said. The issue arose when Nashik-based trader NG Thakkar & Sons challenged the APMC’s collection of market fees under Section 31 of the Maharashtra Agricultural Produce Marketing (Development & Regulation) Act, 1963. The trading firm wrote to the Director of Marketing that Hing was missing from the specific list of agricultural produce in the notification dated December 8, 2005, as well as the Schedule to the 1963 Act. The Director of Marketing in 2011 ruled in favor of the trader, holding that market fees could not be levied on Hing. This decision was later affirmed in appeal by the Minister of State. The Nashik APMC then approached the High Court, contending that Hing is legally and commercially recognized as a spice. Justice Borkar observed that when the Central Act includes “Asafoetida” in its schedule of spices, the submission that Hing cannot be regarded as a spice at all cannot be accepted. The Court rejected the argument that a commodity must be individually named to be regulated. "

items.title: Delhi HC seeks response from State, DJB on PIL to regularise sewer workers, pay ₹1 crore compensation for death
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday issued notice to the Delhi government and the Delhi Jal Board (DJB) on a public interest litigation (PIL) petition seeking directions to regularise all the sewer workers in the national capital and provide compensation of more than ₹1 crore to the family of every deceased sewer or septic tank worker. The petitioner also sought directions to extend compassionate government employment to one of the dependents of deceased sewer workers. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia directed the government authorities to collect the relevant data and give complete information to the Court. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The PIL was filed by Dalit Adivasi Shakti Adhikar Manch. As per the plea, sewer workers are among the most economically and socially marginalised sections and are allegedly being paid below minimum wages without benefits such as provident fund, gratuity and bonus. It was argued that sanitation workers continue to suffer from chronic illnesses, permanent disabilities, and occupational diseases caused by repeated exposure to untreated human waste, toxic gases, contaminated water, and unsafe working conditions, which also affects their mental well-being and life expectancy. “Exposure to these gases results in suffocation, unconsciousness, acute respiratory failure, pulmonary oedema, neurological damage, and, in numerous cases, death. Even where exposure is non-fatal, repeated inhalation causes chronic respiratory illnesses, reduced lung capacity, persistent breathlessness, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, recurrent chest infections, and irreversible damage to the respiratory system,” the plea said. Therefore, the petitioner said that there should be complete mechanisation of sewer and septic tank cleaning across Delhi and a prohibition on hazardous manual entry into sewers and manholes. Criminal, departmental and civil action should be initiated against contractors, employers and public officials responsible for violations, it was submitted. The PIL was filed through advocate Umesh Kumar. items.title: Allahabad HC rejects plea questioning Rahul Gandhi's citizenship after petitioner fails to produce evidence
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has refused to entertain a petition challenging Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi's right to be a Member of Parliament (MP) on the ground that he is not a citizen of India [Ashok Pandey and Another v Sri Rahul Gandhi @ Raul Vinci New Delhi and 2 Others] In its order passed on August 31, a bench of Justice Shekhar B Saraf and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary noted that the petitioner failed to produce even a single document to prove his allegation that Gandhi was a citizen of the United Kingdom. Considering the Court's observations, the petitioner chose to withdraw the plea. The request was granted by the Court. "In light of the submission made above, the petitioner is permitted to withdraw the present writ petition. The present writ petition as such is dismissed as withdrawn," the Court said. Justices Shekhar B Saraf and Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary Allahabad High Court Petitioner could not show a single document to show that Rahul Gandhi has declared himself to be a British citizen. The Court had earlier said it was skeptical to entertain the writ petition since the issue related to Gandhi's citizenship was pending before the Central government. However, the Court heard the matter on petitioner's insistence and looked into the documents produced by him. The petitioner had alleged that Gandhi had in 2003 incorporated a UK Based company M/s Backops Limited and declared himself to be a director and major share-holder and also a British national. However, the Court observed that though the petitioner's arguments appeared to be very attractive with far reaching consequences, he could not show a single document on records relating to the formation of the company or the records of Registrar of Companies of Britain or any declaration to show that the "Shri Rahul Gandhi @ Raul Vinci" had declared himself to be a British citizen. "The only document relied upon by the petitioner-in-person is some alleged letter of confirmation issued by University of Cambridge certifying the study of one Raul Vinci, which according to this Court does not in any manner prove any of the allegations being contested in the present petition," the Bench said. Pertinently, a separate petition over Gandhi's alleged British citizenship is pending before another bench of the High Court. Petitioner Rajneesh Kumar Singh appeared in person. items.title: Madras HC appoints former Calcutta HC Chief Justice to decide row over dog show judge
items.summary: The Madras High Court has appointed former Calcutta High Court Chief Justice TS Sivagnanam as an arbitrator to decide a dispute over the appointment of a dog show judge by the Kennel Club of India (KCI). Justice K Kumaresh Babu passed the order on September 1 in a petition filed by one CS Sanjay Reddy, who moved the Court challenging the appointment of one Gauri Nargolkar as an 'all breed judge' of the Kennel Club. Reddy alleged that Nargolkar was elevated to the position without possessing the requisite qualifications. Justice K Kumaresh Babu An 'all breed judge' is a judge qualified to assess dogs belonging to different recognised breeds at dog shows. Reddy had initially filed a civil suit to have Nargolkar’s appointment declared null and void. However, the Kennel Club and the other respondents invoked the arbitration clause in its by-laws and sought reference of the dispute to arbitration under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act. The civil court accepted the plea and referred the dispute to arbitration. Reddy unsuccessfully challenged that decision in appeal and later moved the High Court in second appeal. He eventually opted to pursue arbitration and approached the High Court for appointment of an arbitrator. The Kennel Club opposed the arbitration petition, arguing that it was barred by limitation and that Reddy had failed to issue a notice invoking arbitration under Section 21 of the Arbitration Act. The High Court rejected both objections. It held that Reddy was entitled to exclude the period spent pursuing his appellate remedies while computing limitation. Justice TS Sivagnanam The Court also held that a separate Section 21 notice was unnecessary since the dispute had already been disclosed in the civil suit and it was the respondents themselves who had earlier contended that it should be resolved through arbitration. Finding no impediment to arbitration, Justice Babu appointed Justice Sivagnanam as the sole arbitrator and permitted him to fix his own fee. Justice Sivagnanam had retired as Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court. He was also appointed to head an appellate tribunal dealing with challenges arising from the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in West Bengal. He later resigned from that role . Reddy was represented by advocate VG Suresh Kumar. Senior Advocate R Srinivas , instructed by advocate Mythili Srinivas, appeared for the respondents. items.title: Delhi HC questions argument that  providing 50% reservation for women in DUSU polls will reduce election violence
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday issued notice to the Central government, the University Grants Commission (UGC) and the Delhi University on a plea seeking 50 percent reservation for female students in Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) and College Students’ Union elections. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia asked the respondents to file their responses to the plea. During the hearing of the case, the Court questioned the petitioner's argument that women's reservation for will help reduce the violence associated with the polls. "Are you suggesting that by providing 50 percent reservation [for women], the violence will abate? Are you saying they are less violent? What is this argument?" the Court asked. The matter will be heard next in November. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The High Court was dealing with a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed by one Shabana Hussain. She stated that the University of Delhi has more than one lakh students, but despite the substantial number of female students, their representation in elected student bodies remains disproportionately low. The plea further highlighted that issues concerning women students, including sexual harassment, hostel curfew timings and safety do not receive adequate representation when women are underrepresented in student unions. The counsel for the petitioner pointed out that the parliament has passed a law reserving 33 percent seats in the Lok Sabha for women and similar steps have been taken by the bar associations of the Supreme Court and High Courts as well. However, the Court asked whether there is a legal right to reservation for women candidates in DUSU polls and whether the Court can pass such an order. "We are here to protect your rights. Can we create a right? Where is this right flowing from? Which statute? Which provision of the Delhi University Act provides for reservation? Where is the authority available to us to create a right?" the Court asked. The Court eventually proceeded to issue notice in the matter. The petition was filed through advocate Ashu Bidhuri. items.title: Government has been lackadaisical in addressing NCLT’s problems: Senior Advocate Sanjiv Sen
items.summary: Senior Advocate Sanjiv Sen has criticised the Central government for not being proactive in addressing institutional and infrastructural problems confronting the National Company Law Tribunals (NCLTs). Sen has an extensive commercial law practice, with particular experience in company law, insolvency, taxation and arbitration. He regularly appears before the Supreme Court, High Courts, the NCLT and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT). His insolvency practice has included significant matters involving Jaypee Infratech, Essar Steel and Bhushan Power and Steel. In an interview with Bar & Bench's SN Thyagarajan on the occasion of the tenth anniversary of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), Sen discussed the functioning of the NCLTs and the NCLAT, delays in insolvency proceedings and the treatment of operational creditors. Edited excerpts follow. SN Thyagarajan (SNT): It has been a decade since the NCLT and NCLAT came into being. How do you assess their performance? Have they created an effective tribunal system? Sanjiv Sen (SS) : Speaking personally, I feel that tribunalisation of justice is something I am against in an ideal situation. Ideally, High Courts should hear all matters, including commercial matters, tax matters and the other matters that have been assigned to tribunals. But the High Courts have their own problems. The combined pendency in the High Courts and subordinate courts is more than 5 crore cases. It has been assessed that at the current rate of disposal, it would take more than 3 centuries to clear the present backlog. We cannot remain in a Utopian world. Tribunalisation has, therefore, become necessary for the faster disposal of cases. The NCLT began functioning in 2016 and assumed jurisdiction over company law matters. The IBC came soon thereafter and gave the NCLT its present form. However, after the advent of the IBC, greater emphasis has been placed on insolvency cases rather than pure company law matters. Pure company law cases have been put on the back burner. Those cases are accumulating and are not being disposed of properly. Overall, consolidating these diverse jurisdictions in one tribunal has been a very good move. The NCLT is specialised and compact. It has the necessary wherewithal and gives much shorter dates than the High Courts traditionally did. It is certainly a good and welcome step to have one tribunal deciding all these matters. items.title: Driving at high speed alone not rash or negligent driving: Delhi High Court
items.summary: Vehicles are intended to be driven fast and the fact that a vehicle was moving at high speed does not, by itself, establish criminal rashness or negligence on the part of the driver, the Delhi High Court recently observed [State v Sanjay] . Justice Chandrasekharan Sudha made the observation while dismissing the Delhi government’s appeal against the acquittal of a tempo driver booked under Sections 279 (rash driving) and 304A (causing death by negligence) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) for causing a woman’s death in a road accident in 2009. “ Vehicles are intended to be driven in speed. Merely because the vehicle was driven at high speed would not mean that the driver was rash or negligent by itself. ‘High speed’ or ‘over speed’ are relative terms, ” the Court said. Justice Chandrasekharan Sudha Delhi High Court Merely because the vehicle was driven at high speed would not mean that the driver was rash or negligent by itself. The case arose from an accident on November 12, 2009. The prosecution alleged that the accused was driving a tempo rashly and negligently when it struck a bicycle carrying a man and his mother near Naresh Park Extension in Delhi. The tempo’s front wheel allegedly ran over the woman’s head, killing her on the spot. A magistrate acquitted the driver in August 2013. The State challenged the decision before the High Court in 2016. The deceased woman’s son, who was riding the bicycle, was the prosecution’s sole witness. He testified that the tempo was being driven at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner. However, the High Court found that he did not explain how the driving was rash or negligent. He was also unable to give even an approximate estimate of the tempo’s speed. “ Mere occurrence of a road traffic incident, which results in a fatality, cannot ipso facto lead to an inference of rashness or negligence on the part of the driver, ” the Court said. The prosecution was required to produce material explaining what constituted high speed in the circumstances of the case, the Court added. In the absence of such material, rashness or negligence could not be presumed by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur . The Court also highlighted inconsistencies in the prosecution’s case. items.title: Elephants have rights: Karnataka High Court quashes land acquisition for housing project near Bannerghatta
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed the acquisition of over 1,938 acres of land for the 4th phase of Suryanagar housing project by Karnataka Housing Board (KHB), holding that the project would have irreversible ecological and wildlife-related consequences [Puttarajamma v State of Karnataka] . A division bench of Justices DK Singh and H Shanthi Bhushan passed the judgment while allowing the appeals filed by the landowners against the acquisition of their agricultural land for Suryanagar 4th Phase Layout. The Court observed that while the Suryanagar project seeks to provide affordable and planned housing plots, it would deprive the wildlife of their natural habitat. It added that the project would seriously affect the Karadikkal-Madeshwara Corridor for elephants. “The elephants in question, for whom these corridors constitute not merely a passage but an essential part of their natural habitat and existence, cannot be treated as occupants without rights whose homes may be displaced at will,” the Bench said. Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan Karnataka High Court Elephants in question cannot be treated as occupants without rights. Accordingly, the Court set aside the decision of a single-bench, which had only partly interfered with the acquisition of land on January 13, 2025. "The entire land acquisition proceedings are nothing but an exercise without undertaking the relevant considerations such as, scientific study of environment impact assessment, socio-ecological factors etc., as flagged by the CEC," the Court ruled. The KHB had initially proposed acquisition of 2,220 acres and two guntas. Following objections by landowners, the State in 2015 issued notifications covering 1,938 acres and 13 guntas. The project involved the acquisition of land in Konasandra, Bommandahalli, Kadujakkanahalli, Indlawadi and Bagganadoddi villages in Anekal taluk. State Environment Impact Assessment Authority granted clearance for the project in 2023. However, the decision was challenged by landowners who, among other things, argued that their agricultural land was the source of their livelihood. It was also argued that the acquisition raised serious environmental concerns in view of the project's proximity to Bannerghatta National Park. The single-judge on January 13, 2025, partly allowed their petitions. items.title: Karnataka HC slaps ₹1 lakh costs on man who lodged email complaint with CJI and ED Director against ED officer
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has imposed costs of ₹1 lakh on a litigant who had marked the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and the Delhi High Court Chief Justice on an email seeking the removal of an Enforcement Directorate (ED) officer from an ongoing investigation [ Fair Vakkayil John Vs Union of India ]. The July 25 email was sent to the ED Director's office, accusing an investigating officer of bias and seeking his recusal from the probe. Copies of the email were forwarded to the CJI, the Delhi High Court Chief Justice, the Finance Minister and the ED's Chief Vigilance Officer. Justice Suraj Govindaraj took note of this while dealing with the litigant's writ petition seeking the High Court's intervention in the same issue. The Court, however, found that the petitioner did not place any material to back up his allegations of bias against the ED's investigating officer. "Except making a general allegation that the Investigating Officer is prejudiced against him, no material has been placed before this Court which would prima facie justify an inference that the investigation is actuated by mala fides or that the Investigating Officer has disabled himself from conducting a fair investigation. Justice Suraj Govindraj The Court further strongly reprimanded the manner in which the petitioner had ventilated his grievances by forwarding his email representation to constitutional functionaries. “This Court is unable to approve either the substance of the representation or the manner in which it has been addressed... The Court was dealing with a plea raising concerns about the fairness of an Assistant Director of the ED in conducting an ongoing probe. The petitioner, Fair Vakkayil John, claimed that he had a reasonable apprehension that the present IO was biased and would not conduct a fair investigation. items.title: Move Andhra Pradesh HC: Delhi High Court rejects PIL against closure of old Visakhapatnam airport
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday rejected a public interest litigation (PIL) petition challenging the closure of Visakhapatnam airport at Dega after commercial operations were transferred to the new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia asked the petitioner, Gopala Krishna Kosaraju, to agitate his grievance before the Andhra Pradesh High Court. The Bench said that since the dominant cause of action arose in Andhra Pradesh, the petitioner must approach the jurisdictional High Court. "Petition dismissed on the ground of forum convenience. It is needless to say that the petitioner will be at liberty to agitate his case before the jurisdictional High Court," the Court ordered. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The old Visakhapatnam airport at INS Dega, which had handled scheduled commercial flights for decades, ceased such operations last month. The shutdown followed the inauguration of the new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram on August 1. All scheduled passenger flights were transferred to the new airport, while INS Dega remains available for non-scheduled and military operations. Advocate Pranav Sachdeva appeared for the petitioner and argued that the new airport is nearly 60 Km from the city of Visakhapatnam and takes over two hours to reach. "There is no connectivity, and the people are suffering. The existing airport was built with thousands of crores of rupees," he said. items.title: Supreme Court seeks structured plan to fix vacancies, pendency in district and state consumer commissions
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed all States to respond within 3 weeks to a status report submitted by Amicus Curiae highlighting vacancies in district and state consumer commissions. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also directed States to explain compliance with its July 22, 2026 order on pay and allowances for commission members. The Court said that the report submitted by the NCDRC President requires serious consideration. Key concerns raised in the report included the appointment process for commission members and the transition to a new enactment, with members under the old regime continuing only until September 6. Attorney General R Venkataramani suggested that selection processes which had begun under the old law may be completed subject to the terms and conditions prescribed under the new enactment. "No tribunal should become non-functional merely because of the transition," the CJI said. The matter is expected to be taken up again on September 8. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The Court was hearing a suo motu case initiated by it to examine nationwide vacancies, staff shortages and mounting pendency in consumer commissions. On rising pendency, NCDRC alone has close to 18,000 pending cases, the report by NCDRC president stated. The AG flagged the restricted use of single-member benches. items.title: Expedite process to fill RERA vacancies: Delhi High Court directs Delhi government
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday directed the Delhi government to expedite the process of filling vacancies in Delhi's Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA). A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia directed the government to file an affidavit regarding the appointments in two weeks. "We direct that the process of filling up the posts be expedited...File an affidavit in two weeks...See to it that at least the judicial members are appointed," the Court said. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The Bench passed the order after two advocates - Aishwary Jain and Deeptanshu Jain - approached the High Court seeking a direction permitting outgoing Delhi RERA Chairperson Anand Kumar to continue in office on an interim, stop-gap basis until a successor is appointed. It was stated that the Chairperson's post fell vacant on August 11, 2026, after Kumar turned 65, while a member's post has been vacant since December 2025. The petitioners allege that no reference has been made to the Selection Committee under Rule 17 of the Delhi RERA Rules, 2016, making it impossible to meet the 90-day selection timeline mandated under Section 24(3) of the RERA Act. Senior Advocate Sanjeev Sagar appeared for the petitioners and argued that RERA must consist of a Chairperson, a judicial member and a technical member, but the Chairperson and judicial member have demitted office, leaving only a technical member. Counsel appearing for the Delhi government informed the Bench that the proposal to extend the tenure of the outgoing chairperson had been rejected on August 11 and the process to appoint a new chairperson was underway. Further, the counsel said that the selection process for filling the post of the judicial member is complete and the government is awaiting the selection committee’s recommendation. items.summary: The Bombay High Court recently quashed a Pune family court order granting ₹10 lakhs as permanent alimony to a woman, after finding the family court based its decision purely on "guesswork" of her estranged husband’s income. In the absence of proper income details, he family court judge had assumed that the husband earned ₹1 lakh per month since he was a skilled and qualified person who had earlier worked in Germany. A Division Bench of Justices Bharati Dangre and Ashish S Chavan strongly disapproved of this approach, observing that the family court judge had carried out such guesswork without any evidence. "The learned Judge has merely carried out a guess work without any evidence produced on record as to what is the earning of the husband and what is the need of the wife," the High Court observed. Justices Bharati Dangre and Ashish S Chavan The High Court, therefore, remanded the matter back to the family court for fresh adjudication. It directed the family court judge to determine the amount of permanent alimony by drawing a statement of the earnings of the husband and the needs of the wife. “ We deem it appropriate to remand the matter back to the Judge, Family Court, Pune, for determination of the amount of permanent alimony as well as the amount of maintenance to be paid to the daughter, which would necessarily have to be commensurate with the earnings of the appellant since the learned Judge has merely carried out a guess work without any evidence produced on record as to what is the earning of the husband and what is the need of the wife,” the Court ordered. The husband had approached the family court with a plea for divorce on the grounds of cruelty. The wife had not defended the case. The court had dissolved the marriage and directed the husband to pay ₹10 lakh as permanent alimony. It also ordered ₹10,000 per month for child maintenance. The husband filed a plea before the High Court challenging the financial directions. He objected to the manner in which the family court had speculated on how much he was earning as income. “ In absence of details, it can be assumed that the petitioner's net income must be ₹1 lakh a month," the family court had ruled. The High Court bench found this approach unacceptable. It stated that permanent alimony and maintenance would have to be commensurate with the actual earnings of the husband. items.title: India's Got Latent row: Supreme Court quashes FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahbadia, others
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday quashed criminal cases filed against digital creator and podcast host Ranveer Allahbadia, and YouTuber-comedians Samay Raina, Ashish Chanchlani and four others over their controversial remarks during an episode of comedy talent show, India's Got Latent. A Bench Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order. Apart from Allahbadia, Raina, and Chanchlani, the others who have been given relief in connection with this case are Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar alias Sonali Aditya Desai, and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar. The Court today also appreciated the efforts made by Raina, Goyal, Ghai, Thakkar and Tanwar to organise shows for the benefit of persons with disabilities. " Once there are genuine efforts positive results are bound to be there. They are very bright youngsters. If they have started working in positive direction, there will be positive output," the Bench said. The Court proceeded to quash criminal cases filed against Raina, Goyal, Ghai, Thakkar and Tanwar over insensitive remarks made on the show against disabled persons. The Court, however, will hear the matter further to consider suggestions from persons with disabilities on how to ensure better checks on such content and frame appropriate directions on the broader issues involved.' items.title: Telangana police constable suspended for abusive remarks against TRS chief Kavitha
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A Telangana police constable, K Anil, was suspended for allegedly posting misogynistic, sexually abusive remarks on social media against Telangana Rakshana Sena (TRS) president and former MP Kalvakuntla Kavitha. Cyberabad Commissioner of Police M Ramesh issued the suspension order against Anil, an Armed Reserve (AR) police constable, on September 2. Earlier the same day, a complaint was submitted to Telangana Director General of Police (DGP), seeking criminal and departmental action against Anil for his comments on Kavitha on a social media post. The complaint, submitted by TRS members, alleged that the constable circulated the objectionable remarks on Facebook, X and other social media platforms. Seeking registration of an FIR, the complainant invoked provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including those relating to insulting the modesty of a woman, sexual harassment and criminal defamation, besides applicable provisions of the Information Technology (IT) Act. Terming the conduct particularly serious as the accused is a serving police official, the petition described it as “conduct unbecoming of a member of the police force” and sought immediate departmental action. It also requested suspension pending inquiry and removal or dismissal from service if the allegations are proved. The complaint also sought preservation of digital evidence, including screenshots, URLs, account details and server records, and forensic examination of devices used to publish the content.

The move comes after CM Revanth and Surekha both visited Delhi and met with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and other party leaders. A recommendation to this effect has already been sent to the Governor, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office. Surekha had faced action from the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC)’s disciplinary committee after her daughter, Susmita, made critical remarks against CM Revanth in August, for the second time in a year. Surekha held the Environment & Forests and Endowment portfolios. She was one of two women Ministers in the Cabinet, along with Danasari Anasuya (Seethakka), who holds the Panchayat Raj & Rural Development and Women & Child Welfare portfolios. The current strength of the Telangana Cabinet is 16, including the Chief Minister, against the maximum permitted strength of 18. The Chief Minister has also decided to rescind the appointment of G Chinna Reddy as Vice Chairman, Telangana Planning Board. Chinna Reddy had also faced action from the disciplinary committee for threatening to revolt against the party leadership, lashing out at CM Revanth for not being given a ticket from Wanaparthy in the 2023 Assembly elections. He will be replaced by Gadwal Vijayalakshmi, who is currently chairperson of the Telangana State Women‘s Commission and former Mayor of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC). Jaleel said Kanthapuram’s remarks should be understood in the context of concerns among sections of the Muslim community over the conduct and positions of women associated with the Indian Union Muslim league (IUML). items.title: NLSIU convocation: Mediation effort hits roadblock, matter now before general council
items.summary: Attempts by National Law School University of India (NLSIU) alumni to mediate between the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and the graduating batch to organise a convocation have been infructuous so far. On August 27, the institute’s registrar had announced that the convocation which was to be held on September 12 had been cancelled. A meeting of the university’s general council will now likely take a decision on the matter. The cancellation of the NLSIU convocation was the fallout of developments stemming from Hyderabad NALSAR students objecting to CJI Surya Kant attending their convocation. Bar Council of India (BCI) Manan Kumar Mishra went on to threaten to prevent NALSAR students’ enrollment in the bar. At the time, NLSIU students, extending solidarity with NALSAR, had objected to the CJI and BCI chief being part of their convocation. The CJI is the chancellor of NLSIU. The BCI chairperson presides over the general council meetings. The general council is empowered to decide on broad policies and programmes of the NLSIU. In other premier law universities in the country, the chief justices of the respective states’ high courts also serve as the chancellor. An alumnus who spoke to TNM on condition of anonymity said that after the convocation was cancelled, the CJI had expressed the sentiment that he was in favour of a swift resolution to the issue. The mediation attempt during the August 29-30 weekend involved conducting another poll seeking the opinion of the graduating batch on whether they were open to issuing a formal statement or whether to have the CJI nominate another judge to attend the convocation in his stead. Of the 324 students in the graduating batch, 205 participated in the poll. Of these 54% were in favour of nominating another judge while the remaining 45% were in favour of the CJI himself attending the event. However, the latter option came with a rider that the students would still have to issue a statement—which need not be a retraction of their previous statement expressing solidarity with the NALSAR students—but an acknowledgement that a conversation took place. items.title: Ex-bureaucrat picked up on morning walk, released 12 hours later
items.summary: Questions about Joshi’s whereabouts began to be raised on social media as soon as news of the pick-up spread. Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit wrote on X: “I came to know about this when his wife spoke to me in the morning. We have been trying to find out where he is since 10 am, but there is no clue. We are very worried, and the Delhi Police should tell us at the earliest where he has been taken.” A Delhi Police officer, speaking on condition of anonymity, said a case was already registered against Joshi at the Special Cell and that he had been brought in for questioning in connection with it. “He was not arrested. He was released after questioning,” the officer said. The officer did not share details about the case. Joshi is a 1992-batch officer of the Indian Post and Telecommunication Accounts and Finance Service. He lives in Moti Bagh and walks in Nehru Park every morning. He had driven there on Wednesday as usual and was walking with friends when the two police personnel approached him and took him away. It emerged later in the day that he had been taken to the Special Cell office in New Friends Colony. A friend of Joshi’s who had gone to the New Friends Colony police station confirmed his release. “We were standing at one gate, and Joshi was taken out from another gate. We were waiting for him at the gate the whole time,” he said. His associates said the family was given no notice at any point, and that if an FIR has been registered against Joshi, its contents have not been shared with them either. Joshi’s wife, daughter and several associates spent the day anxious and in the dark about his whereabouts. It was only in the evening that they learned where he was and arrived at the station to pick him up. His family could not be reached for comment. After reaching home, Joshi posted on X: “Just reached home. The Delhi Special Cell has dropped me home. I will share the rest of the details later.” Reached for comment, Joshi said several people had come to the house and that he would speak later. items.title: ₹20 lakh bill after Rapido bike crash: Bengaluru woman’s fight for accountability
items.summary: A Rapido bike taxi ride in Bengaluru left Sani Krishna with nine broken ribs, multiple surgeries and medical bills exceeding ₹20 lakh. She says she has not received any compensation from the company so far. Sani alleges the rider tried to overtake a tractor before the bike skidded, throwing her into its path. She also says her attempts to seek help from Rapido went unanswered until she spoke publicly about the accident. Now, as she prepares to approach the consumer court, her case raises a larger question: when a passenger is seriously injured during an app-based ride, who is responsible?
